review.title: CI executes every script suite the repository declares, and a failing validate job says something
review.acceptance:
CREATED ON gpt-architect's ROUND-107 DIRECTIVE. Two defects, one file.

A. EVERY SUITE THE REPOSITORY DECLARES IS EXECUTED BY CI. The validate job mirrors `npm run test:scripts` as separate named steps, and its own comment says 'a FIFTH script added to it must be added here too' -- and then records that the drift it warns about had already happened once. It has happened twice more: `test:scripts` now names SIX scripts and this job runs FOUR of them. `scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs` and `node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs` (30 cases) are in the alias and in no step. `apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs` (17 cases) is in no alias and no step and is run by nothing at all.
REQUIRED: all three execute in CI and fail the build when they fail.
REQUIRED: the mirror is kept in step BY A MECHANISM, not by a comment asking a human to remember. A note that a hand-kept list must be kept in step is already in the file, it did not keep the list in step, and a fourth occurrence of the same drift is not a thing to apologise for again.
REQUIRED: the added suites run where their dependencies allow. The six pre-install steps are pre-install on purpose -- they use Node builtins only, so a dependency failure cannot mask a control-plane or structure failure -- and a suite placed there must actually hold to that.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: 'do not turn apps/desktop into a workspace if that causes validators to traverse generated packaging output'. Round 106 measured exactly that and it does: a dependency-free apps/desktop/package.json costs 8 lockfile lines and turbo picks the suite up, but `validate-workspace-deps.mjs` then walks apps/desktop/sidecar/server/ -- generated packaging output carrying its own .gitignore of '*' -- and demands the manifest declare `next`. The measurement is in coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md section 8.

B. A FAILING `validate` JOB SAYS SOMETHING ACTIONABLE. On run 37028642916 at 30cef6e the job aborted at 10m 38s with one annotation, 'Process completed with exit code 134', naming no step -- having PASSED at 25m 4s and 27m 29s on the two runs before it. Exit 134 is SIGABRT. The engineering session cannot read run logs or download artifacts (the Actions API answers 403) and so could not determine which step aborted, let alone why; two local reproductions of the prime suspect passed, at 1261s ambient and 1807s under a runner-like heap cap.
REQUIRED: a run page carries enough to tell a reader WHICH step aborted and under what machine conditions -- at minimum core count, total and available memory, free disk, the Node version and NODE_OPTIONS -- without needing the log or the artifact.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: 'DO NOT declare OOM. DO NOT increase memory merely because exit 134 occurred. DO NOT increase timeouts without evidence. DO NOT add retries to hide it. Improve diagnostics first.' Nothing in this task may change what CI runs or how much it is given. Diagnostics only.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: no secret leakage. Nothing added here may print the environment wholesale, a token, or a value this repository has not already published; an allowlist of named variables, never a dump.

C. THE JOB'S COST DOES NOT GROW MATERIALLY. The three added suites take under a second between them locally. Diagnostics must stay cheap enough that nobody is tempted to remove them the next time the job is slow.

WHAT IS DEMONSTRABLY READABLE IS AN ANNOTATION, and every CI fact this project has obtained came from one. So the three facts that matter are now emitted as workflow commands as well, with the summary kept for a human reading in a browser:
  ::warning "validate failed"    -- the first failing step, derived from the step ids;
  ::notice  "validate machine"   -- cores, memory, free disk, node, npm and NODE_OPTIONS, BEFORE and AFTER on one line, which is what makes either number mean anything;
  ::warning "V8 fatal error"     -- the redactor's new --line mode, same allowlist rendered on one line.

EXECUTED UNDER GITHUB'S OWN SHELL FLAGS (bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail), three branches, each exit 0:
  - with a V8 report present: all three annotations emitted, the V8 one carrying event, trigger, heap limit/committed/used, external, rss, peak rss, free and total memory, cpu seconds and the entry script;
  - with no report and no facts file: the machine annotation says "BEFORE not recorded" rather than failing, and no V8 annotation is emitted;
  - runner-facts writes its file and its summary, exit 0.
THE ALLOWLIST STILL HOLDS ON THE NEW PATH, tested as an attack: a process aborted with SECRET_TOKEN=hunter2 in its environment leaves the value once in the raw diagnostic report and ZERO times in the emitted annotation. The raw report is still never printed and never uploaded.

ANNOTATIONS ARE KEPT FEW AND SHORT -- three, each truncated at 380 characters -- because they are capped and truncated by GitHub, and a verdict cut in half is worse than a short one. The step-by-step table stays in the summary where length is free.

AND THE CORRECTION THAT WEAKENS THIS TASK'S ORIGINAL JUSTIFICATION, repeated here because it belongs with the evidence: rounds 106 and 107 said the annotation "names an exit code and no step". It names the step -- on the JOB page, which needs no login; the RUN page drops the attribution, and that is the page both rounds read. Run 37036128012's validate job says exit 134 under "Test AI control plane". The comment in ci.yml asserting the limitation is corrected in the file, and what the step-outcome table is still worth is stated narrowly there: it separates a step that FAILED from one that never STARTED, and it survives a job that ends with no annotation at all.

LOCAL RE-VERIFICATION: ci.yml parses, 20 steps; the mirror check passes against the repaired file; the moved suite passes where it now runs.

review.title: The watchlist harness reads a rate-limited sign-UP as a wrong password
review.acceptance:
THE OBSERVATION, WHICH IS FACT. CI run 37036128012 at 2c037d54ed834af9dba3c6b12a29c395dee81b9d: the e2e job failed, PRODUCTION mode only, 1 failed / 75 passed / 31 skipped, on 'tests/watchlist.spec.ts:859:7 - the list page, against a real session and a real database - a signed-in viewer with no profile selected is sent to the picker, not to an error'. The annotation is the harness's own message: 'the harness could not sign in as e2e-watchlist-unchosen-0@liberty.invalid: 401 {"message":"Invalid email or password","code":"INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD"}'. The DEVELOPMENT run in the same job passed, 93 passed / 14 skipped. The same spec passed in production on the previous run, 37028642916 at 30cef6e, 76 passed / 31 skipped, and nothing between those two commits touches authentication, the harness or the spec -- so it is intermittent rather than a break.

THE DEFECT IN THE HARNESS, WHICH IS ALSO FACT AND IS VISIBLE IN THE SOURCE REGARDLESS OF WHAT CAUSED THIS RUN. `signIn` in that file POSTs /api/auth/sign-up/email with failOnStatusCode: false and never looks at the response -- the comment says the sign-in is what decides, 'because a session is what the caller asked for and an account is only the way to get one'. It then retries the SIGN-IN on 429 up to four times and on nothing else. So a sign-up that was refused leaves no account, the sign-in that follows correctly answers 401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD because better-auth does not distinguish an unknown user from a wrong password, and the harness reports a credential failure for an account that was never created. The retry loop makes this worse rather than better: it waits out a rate-limit window and then re-asks a question whose answer cannot change.
REQUIRED: a sign-up that fails is OBSERVED and reported as itself. A 401 must not be the error text for 'the account does not exist'.
REQUIRED: whatever retry the sign-up is given is the same client-correctness retry the sign-in already has -- obeying a 429 and its retry-after. playwright.config.ts's rule stands: no ASSERTION is retried, retries stay 0, and the fix must not be `retries: 1` on the project.
REQUIRED: the diagnosis is CONFIRMED before the repair is called a repair. The hypothesis in the notes is a hypothesis.
REQUIRED: the repair is demonstrated against the production + real PostgreSQL configuration, which is the only one that failed; a development-mode pass proves nothing here, because that is the configuration that was already green.

OUT OF SCOPE AND MUST NOT BE DONE: deleting or skipping the test, relaxing its assertion, serialising the project, raising a timeout, or changing the application's authentication configuration to make the harness's traffic acceptable. The product's rate limiting is a security property; a test harness that trips it is the harness's problem.
review.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 107 from CI run 37036128012. NOT CAUSED BY THIS ROUND'S WORK: the delta from the last green e2e is one apps/desktop packaging script, two coordination documents and control-plane state.

THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS, LABELLED AS ONE BECAUSE IT HAS NOT BEEN CONFIRMED. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts passes no `rateLimit` option, so better-auth's default applies -- and that default is ENABLED IN PRODUCTION AND DISABLED IN DEVELOPMENT, which is exactly the split this failure shows. If the per-path default on the sign-up endpoint is short-windowed, several Playwright workers establishing sessions in parallel would exceed it, the refused sign-up would be swallowed by the code above, and the sign-in would answer 401. That fits every observed fact and is still a guess: nobody has watched the sign-up endpoint return 429 under this harness. Confirm it by observation before building on it, and if it is wrong, say so and file what was actually found.

SHAPE NOTE. This is PL-0713 again in a different costume -- a harness that works at one worker and one machine and reports a product failure when the schedule changes. The lesson PL-0713 recorded applies: the repair is structural isolation, not a retry.

CONFLICTS, BOTH FIELDS BOTH DIRECTIONS, AT FILING. e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts is in PW-0304's and PW-0313's allowedPaths and both are DONE; e2e/** was PL-0501's and it is DONE. e2e/src/identity.ts is PW-0312's, DONE. No open task holds any of these in either field. The active tasks at filing are PW-0208 (REVIEW), PW-0602 (IN_PROGRESS) and PL-0714 (IN_PROGRESS), and none names an e2e path.

ROUND 108 SURFACE AMENDMENT, recorded as an event before any write: e2e/src/identity.ts moved from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths. The production reproduction at 4 workers failed on HARNESS_ACCOUNT in that file, not on the watchlist slot -- the two carry the identical defect, and repairing only the one CI happened to show would leave the one that actually reproduces.

typecheck.evidence: e2e/ npx tsc --noEmit: clean, after both files changed. Two type imports added (APIResponse in each); nothing else in the harness's types moved.

e2e.evidence:
THE DIAGNOSIS WAS CONFIRMED BEFORE THE REPAIR WAS CALLED A REPAIR, which the acceptance requires, and the confirmation moved the fix.

READ OUT OF THE INSTALLED LIBRARY. better-auth 1.7.5, dist/context/create-context.mjs line 172: `enabled: options.rateLimit?.enabled ?? isProduction` -- rate limiting is ON in production and OFF in development, which is exactly the split the CI failure showed. dist/api/rate-limiter/index.mjs getDefaultSpecialRules: window 10 seconds, max 3, for any path beginning /sign-in or /sign-up, keyed per IP and path. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts passes no rateLimit option, so that default is what the application runs.

REPRODUCED, in the configuration the acceptance names as decisive. Production mode, real PostgreSQL 16 on 127.0.0.1:5433 with the repository migration applied, COLD DATABASE so every worker must create its account, --workers=4, full chromium+api suite: 12 failed, and the auth failure is "the harness could not sign in as e2e-harness-2@liberty.invalid: 401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD". A single-worker run of the same suite passes, which is why this was invisible on a two-core machine -- the same thing that hid PL-0713.

THE REPRODUCTION MOVED THE REPAIR, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH READING. The failing account is e2e-harness-2, which is src/identity.ts's HARNESS_ACCOUNT -- NOT the watchlist slot CI happened to hit. The two files carry the identical defect line for line. Fixing only the one named in the CI annotation would have left the one that actually reproduces here. The surface was amended to include e2e/src/identity.ts, recorded as an event before the write and conflict-checked in both fields in both directions.

THE REPAIR, IN BOTH FILES.
  - SIGN IN FIRST. A database that already has the account costs one request and the burst never happens. This is the change that removes the pressure rather than tolerating it.
  - The sign-up response is OBSERVED. "Already exists" is treated as success -- the account this harness needs is there either way -- and every other refusal throws, naming that the account does not exist so that nothing downstream is about a password.
  - A 429 is obeyed on BOTH endpoints, honouring X-Retry-After, on the same bounded budget the sign-in already had. SIGN_IN_ATTEMPTS was NOT raised.
  - Every attempt is logged and the log is in the failure message, so the next occurrence names itself.

THE REGRESSION RUN, SAME DECISIVE CONFIGURATION. Production mode, real PostgreSQL, cold database, --workers=4, full chromium+api suite: 77 PASSED, 41 skipped, 0 FAILED. No sign-in failure of any kind. Development mode, full suite: 103 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, EACH FORBIDDEN BY THE ACCEPTANCE AND NONE OF THEM TEMPTING ONCE THE CAUSE WAS KNOWN: no test deleted or skipped, no assertion relaxed, no project serialised, no timeout raised, no retry count changed -- playwright.config.ts is untouched and `retries` is still 0 -- and NOTHING in the application's rate limiting was configured, relaxed or disabled. Obeying a 429 is correct client behaviour; the file says so at length, and it is the server stating a protocol requirement rather than an assertion being re-evaluated.

A FINDING FOR THE BOARD, NOT FIXED HERE: the application's auth rate limiting is better-auth's UNEXAMINED DEFAULT. Nobody chose 3-per-10-seconds, nobody chose that it is off in development, and docs/SECURITY.md residual risk R2 still says "No rate limit on any route". PL-0716 corrected the readiness item to say so precisely; deciding what the limit SHOULD be is a security task that does not exist yet.

review.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
review.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.
review.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

build.evidence: npm run build (turbo) at 95d8b7658065b4c52699d6e0882ed7d04a119a21: Tasks 12 successful, 12 total, exit 0. STATED PLAINLY: 11 of 12 were cache hits, because this task's surface is apps/desktop/scripts, docs/LICENSING.md and a coordination document, and none of that is a build input for any workspace. A build gate on a change the build graph cannot see is close to vacuous and saying otherwise would be a green mark that means nothing. WHAT ACTUALLY EXERCISES THIS ROUND'S CODE: node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs, 17 cases, 0 failures, covering the three historical shapes of a manifest licence field, the four evidence verdicts, the filename pattern, and the rendered document's ordering, timestamp-freedom, escaping and written-offer text. collect-notices.mjs exercised end to end against a synthetic packaged tree: scoped packages, the legacy { type } manifest shape, a LICENSE-MIT file, a package with no evidence at all, and --strict exiting 1. The runtime-licence copy verified BOTH WAYS -- the generated notices carry 'No LICENSE accompanied this binary' when none is present and do not when one is. node --check on package-sidecar.mjs, collect-notices.mjs, notices.mjs and notices.test.mjs. Also clean at the same commit: npm run lint 12/12 with 0 errors (1 pre-existing warning in PW-0313's surface), npm run repo:validate, npm run ai:validate (114 tasks). THE TEST FOUND A REAL BUG IN THE FIRST ATTEMPT: the licence-filename pattern allowed only an extension, so a dual-licensed package shipping LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE would have been reported as carrying no licence text at all. UNVERIFIED AND NOT CLAIMED: no libmpv or FFmpeg build was produced -- this container's toolchains target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- and the notices generator has never run against a real packaged tree, because packaging happens on Windows. What the real dependency list will say is a thing the first Windows packaging run prints and nobody here can predict.

review.title: A player that can actually be operated
review.acceptance: The player has controls. TODAY IT HAS NONE: player-surface.tsx sets the native controls attribute on a video element and renders a debug panel, and its own header says 'NO CONTROLS ARE BUILT HERE'. There is no play, pause, seek, volume, fullscreen, subtitle, audio, quality or source control anywhere in this product. REQUIRED: play/pause, a seek bar with buffered ranges, volume and mute, fullscreen, a subtitle menu and an audio-track menu driven by PW-0206, and a source/quality state the viewer can read. REQUIRED: keyboard operation -- space, arrows, F, M, and Escape -- because there is not one keyboard handler in the entire application today and a Windows media application that cannot be driven from the keyboard is not finished. REQUIRED: an idle-hide overlay that never hides a control from a keyboard or screen-reader user. REQUIRED: the controls layer sends no side effect the state machine does not already own; playback-effects.ts deliberately exposes four effects and its header says FOUR, AND NO MORE, so a control that needs a fifth is a machine change with its own justification. REQUIRED: the controls read the adapter, not Shaka, so the same UI operates the native engine.
review.notes:
PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. 

ROUND 108 SURFACE AMENDMENT, recorded as task.definition_changed before any write. The adapter boundary and the Shaka adapter join the write surface -- four named files, all previously PW-0206's and now unowned -- because two acceptance clauses are unreachable without them: PlayerAdapter cannot report BUFFERED RANGES at all, and it cannot report TRACKS unless it performed the load, which it did not and must not. Routing the load through the adapter was rejected on a RIGHTS ground: PlayerSession candidates carry protection and compatibility, the client PlaybackSession carries neither, and projecting one into the other would mean inventing a rights-bearing fact. That reconciliation is PW-0203's by the round-82 ruling and was not taken. Instead the boundary gains two READS -- resynchronise(), which the boundary already anticipated (the resynchronised event exists and PW-0204 requires mpv to resynchronise from properties on queue overflow) and getBufferedRanges(), beside the three pull-side reads already there. player-adapter.ts moved from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths; it was already inside the reviewed surface, so this widens the write surface and not the fingerprint. The e2e gate needed a path: e2e/tests/player-controls.spec.ts was added to the surface in the same round, one new file, because vitest here runs with environment "node" and a keyboard clause cannot be evidenced without a keyboard.

HOW THE WORK IS SPLIT, BECAUSE apps/web HAS NO DOM. vitest.config.ts sets environment "node", so no effect runs, no keystroke is dispatched and no menu opens. The same observation PW-0307 made one task earlier, used the same way:

WHAT I ADDED THIS ROUND ON TOP OF THE IMPLEMENTATION ALREADY IN THE TREE, and it is the clause that was missing rather than a polish pass.

PW-0206 WAS STILL UNREACHABLE. Its module -- the normalised vocabulary, the identity, reapply, rememberChoice -- was imported by NOTHING. PL-0716's readiness audit had to score track selection PARTIAL for exactly that reason, and this task's acceptance asks for menus "driven by PW-0206". The menus were driven by this task's own trackOptions; the POLICY was not wired at all, so a viewer's choice did not survive a candidate switch -- which is the one clause PW-0206 exists for.
  - controls-state.ts gains restoreCommands() and rememberFromMenu(), pure, which call PW-0206's reapply/rememberChoice. 11 new tests.

  - MUTATION-TESTED RATHER THAN TRUSTED, four plausible wrong implementations, each reverted: remembering the track id instead of the identity (3 failed); dropping the already-selected guard, which would re-command on every candidate switch forever (1); treating a subtitle "off" as "no choice", which would let a default-marked track on the next candidate turn text back on for a viewer who switched it off (2); and a guard written as "restored differs from current" instead of "restored exists and differs from current" (SURVIVED the first four tests -- it only misbehaves when the viewer's language is absent AND another audio track is already selected, where it would command selectAudioTrack(null), which the adapter throws on. A test was added for exactly that case and the mutant now fails).

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A SHORTCUT. resolveTracks -- the DEFAULT selection for a viewer who has chosen nothing -- needs a PlaybackCapabilities, and this layer does not have one and must not invent one. watch-session.ts refuses the same thing in its own words: a capability union assembled by something that cannot see the engines "would be a capability claim nobody measured". Routing a real profile down here is PW-0308's settings work and PL-0502's engine union. Until then the engine's own default plays and the viewer's explicit choice is honoured, which is the honest subset and is stated in the module rather than left to be discovered.

e2e.evidence:
RE-RECORDED, AND THE REASON IS A HOLE IN THE PREVIOUS RECORDING RATHER THAN AN ADDITION TO IT.

THE PREVIOUS e2e GATE REPORTED A DEVELOPMENT-MODE RUN AND DID NOT SAY THAT PRODUCTION WAS UNRUN. It was. Running the full suite in production mode against a real PostgreSQL, which PL-0715's work required anyway, ALL TEN player-controls cases failed at `toHaveCount(1)` on the control bar.

NOT A DEFECT IN THE BAR. On that build /watch answers with a refusal rather than a session -- observed heading "Sign in to watch this", because the harness's browser context is anonymous and authentication refuses before the catalog is consulted -- so there is no player, and a bar that had rendered anyway would have been the row of buttons wired to nothing that player-surface.tsx renders conditionally to prevent. The ten cases were simply written as though development were the only configuration.

THE REPAIR, WHICH FOLLOWS THE RULE PW-0601 AND docs/TEST_MATRIX.md ALREADY STATE -- a row that does not run says why BY NAME. The ten operation cases stand down when CATALOG_AVAILABILITY is "refused", through a single guard inside the shared openPlayer helper so the reason cannot drift between them, and the reason names what was actually observed. An ELEVENTH case runs in their place in exactly that configuration and asserts what is true there: the route answers 200, it renders a visible non-empty refusal heading, and NO CONTROL BAR PRETENDS OTHERWISE.

TWO DRAFTS OF THAT ELEVENTH CASE WERE WRONG AND A PRODUCTION RUN CORRECTED BOTH -- recorded because the second is the interesting one. It first asserted an h1; PlaybackUnavailable renders an h2, the route frame owning the h1. It then asserted the heading matched /playback|play/, and the heading it met was "Sign in to watch this" -- authentication refusing before the catalog. WHICH refusal is therefore deliberately not pinned: there are four, the one reached depends on configuration this case does not control, and pinning one would make a test about the player fail the next time a deployment's reason changed.

THE RUNS, BOTH MODES, AFTER EVERY CHANGE THIS ROUND.
  development, full chromium+api suite: 103 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed.
  production + real PostgreSQL 16, cold database, --workers=4, full chromium+api suite: 77 passed, 41 skipped, 0 failed. The ten operation cases are among the skips, each naming its reason; the eleventh passes.

THE TEN CASES THEMSELVES ARE UNCHANGED and still cover what they covered: every named control present with an accessible name, the native video chrome gone, the whole bar reachable by TAB in order, SPACE operating the player without scrolling the page, the arrows on volume rather than the page, M mutes and the button says which state it is in, a track menu that opens and announces itself and admits an empty source, ESCAPE closing it, THE BAR NEVER LEAVING THE ACCESSIBILITY TREE however it is dimmed, and the seek bar announcing a TIME rather than a percentage.

STILL NOT ASSERTED, AND THE REASON STILL MATTERS MORE THAN THE OMISSION: that the picture moves, because no real media decodes in this harness; and the re-application of a viewer's track choice across a real candidate switch end to end, because no harness here produces two candidates with real track lists. The decision behind that one has 11 unit tests and four caught mutations; the three lines that issue it are unverified wiring and are named as such.

AND A GAP THIS EXPOSED THAT BELONGS TO NOBODY YET: operating the player on a DEPLOYMENT needs both a configured catalog source and a signed-in viewer, and no spec owns that journey. It is named in the skip reason rather than left for the next person to rediscover.
